0.long_answer: Dumping syndrome is a recognized complication of Nissen fundoplication where the stomach empties its contents too rapidly into the duodenum. This rapid transit can lead to a range of gastrointestinal and vasomotor symptoms, including nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dizziness, and palpitations. The altered physiology post-surgery, due to the fundoplication wrap modifying the gastric reservoir and its emptying dynamics, can predispose some patients to this syndrome. The onset of symptoms typically occurs after eating, particularly following large or high-carbohydrate meals.
